review_locator: PMCID:PMC3121741, Interferon Regulatory Factor 8 Regulates Pathways for Antigen Presentation in Myeloid Cells and during Tuberculosis; PMCID:PMC9454819, IRF8: Mechanism of Action and Health Implications
primary_title: PU.1 and interferon consensus sequence-binding protein regulate the myeloid expression of the human Toll-like receptor 4 gene
decision_basis: The reviews identify TLR4 as an IRF8/PU.1-regulated myeloid gene; the cited primary shows both factors constitutively occupy a composite IRF/Ets element required for maximal human TLR4 promoter activity in macrophages.
limitations_preserved: Direct composite IRF/Ets occupancy and mutation-sensitive promoter activity support a bounded human myeloid IRF8/PU.1-to-TLR4 gene bridge; mouse promoter dependence differs, so preserve species and basal-regulation context without inferring LPS receptor signaling, protein abundance, SCI effects, or terminal-TF output.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC9454819, IRF8: Mechanism of Action and Health Implications; PMCID:PMC3863528, Interferon-Regulatory Factors Determine Macrophage Phenotype Polarization
primary_title: The macrophage IRF8/IRF1 regulome is required for protection against infections and is associated with chronic inflammation
decision_basis: The reviews identify TLR9 as an IRF8/IRF1-coregulated macrophage gene; the cited primary shows IRF8 and IRF1 occupancy at the Tlr9 locus with IFN-gamma-responsive expression reduced in Irf8 and Irf1 mutant macrophages.
limitations_preserved: Co-occupancy and mutant-sensitive IFN-gamma regulation support a bounded IRF8/IRF1 Tlr9 gene bridge in mouse macrophages; preserve STAT1/PU.1 partner context and do not infer TLR9 protein abundance, ligand sensing, SCI effects, or terminal-TF output.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC9454819, IRF8: Mechanism of Action and Health Implications; PMCID:PMC3863528, Interferon-Regulatory Factors Determine Macrophage Phenotype Polarization
primary_title: The macrophage IRF8/IRF1 regulome is required for protection against infections and is associated with chronic inflammation
decision_basis: The reviews identify Nos2 as an IRF8/IRF1-coregulated macrophage gene; the cited primary shows both factors at the Nos2 locus, IFN-gamma-responsive chromatin activation, reduced Nos2 expression in Irf8/Irf1 mutant macrophages and reduced nitric-oxide output.
limitations_preserved: Co-occupancy and mutant-sensitive IFN-gamma regulation support a bounded IRF8/IRF1 Nos2 gene bridge in mouse macrophages; preserve STAT1/PU.1 partner context and distinguish Nos2 transcription from nitric-oxide production, without inferring secretion, SCI effects, or terminal-TF output.
